notes: The parts are the same as in step 1, with no additions or removals.
The black wire runs from the highlighted GND pin (physical pin 9, GND.2 in the catalogue) to breadboard row 15. The purple wire runs from GPIO17 (pin 11) to row 18. Both wire ends sit in column a.
The buzzer body hides its legs. I assumed they go into column e of rows 15 and 18, in the same strips as the wire ends, as the dashed continuation of each wire suggests.
The buzzer's polarity is not shown in the image. I wired the GND row to pin 1 (-) and the GPIO17 row to pin 2 (+), as the catalogue card requires.
No resistor is used, as the tutorial says. The active buzzer is driven directly from GPIO17.
The Pi is modelled as raspberry-pi-3b, which has named GPIO ports. The exact model is not stated in the manual.
